title: Hello and Goodbye
objective: Greet and take leave with the right formula for the time of day and register (hi/hello/good morning/bye/see you).
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you learn to say hello and goodbye in English. Some greetings change with the time of day, and some are only for friends. Careful: 'Good night' is for leaving, not for arriving.]
{{l1_contrast:greetings_pragmatics}}
notes: TODO_audio: exercises 2 and 7 carry the spoken line as written transcript in the prompt ('...' after [audio]); audio assets not yet produced. Register framing: 'best choice' items (ex 5) score the register-appropriate option, they do not mark 'Hi' as ungrammatical.

exercises.prompt: hello · hi · good morning · good evening · good night · goodbye · bye · See you later.
exercises.rationale: Establish form-meaning link with audio for all eight greeting/leave-taking items before any production.

exercises.prompt: [audio] 'Good night!' — [L1: Is the person arriving or leaving?]
exercises.rationale: The single highest-value pragmatic contrast of the lesson: English 'good night' is only a farewell, while es 'buenas noches' is both greeting and farewell.

options.label: [L1: Leaving — it is a farewell.]
options.rationale: 'Good night' is said only when leaving or going to bed.

options.label: [L1: Arriving — it is a greeting.]
options.rationale: Direct es transfer: 'buenas noches' greets AND takes leave; English splits this into 'good evening' (greet) vs 'good night' (leave).

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each expression to when you use it.]

pairs.right: [L1: greeting — at night, when you arrive]
[L1: farewell — before bed or when you leave at night]
[L1: informal greeting — any time, with friends]

exercises.rationale: Maps each formula to time-of-day AND function (greet vs leave) in one pass; isolates the evening/night split introduced in ex 2.

exercises.prompt: [L1: It is 8:00 in the morning. You arrive and greet:] Good ___!
exercises.rationale: First productive selection of the time-bound greeting; 'night' catches the buenas-noches transfer again in production, 'bye' catches greet/leave confusion.

exercises.prompt: [L1: You meet your new teacher for the first time. Which greeting is the best choice?]
exercises.rationale: Register discrimination (band: hi/hello and bye/goodbye are register pairs); learners from small-register-distance greeting cultures often default to the informal form everywhere.

options.label: Hello!
options.rationale: Neutral and safe with a teacher or any new person.

options.label: Hi!
options.rationale: Not wrong, but informal — best kept for friends; the item trains noticing the register pair.

options.label: Bye!
options.rationale: A farewell, not a greeting — catches learners matching sound (short, friendly) instead of function.

exercises.rationale: Assembles the three-word leave-taking chunk; fixed-formula word order must become automatic before it appears inside dialogues.
Fine phonetic discrimination inside the taught set: all three options share sounds with the target, so the learner must hear the whole word, not the first syllable.

options.label: Goodbye!
options.rationale: Two syllables, starts with 'good-' and ends in '-bye'.

options.label: Good night!
options.rationale: Also starts with 'good-'; catches learners who stop listening after the first syllable.

options.label: Bye!
options.rationale: The short register pair of the same word; forces hearing the 'good-' syllable.

exercises.prompt: A: Bye! See you ___!  B: See you!
exercises.rationale: Productive completion of the chunk in a two-turn exchange; the distractors are real words that produce unidiomatic forms ('see you night'), training chunk integrity.

exercises.prompt: [L1: It is morning. Greet your classmate, then say goodbye two ways: one neutral, one informal.]
exercises.rationale: Integrates time-of-day choice plus the register pairs in real time; counts toward guided-interaction minutes.
